record.original_question: Let G be a locally compact group and omega a continuous weight function on G. Is the Beurling algebra L^1(G, omega) approximately amenable, equivalently pseudo-amenable in this bounded-approximate-identity setting, exactly when it is amenable?

evidence.quote: Let omega be a continuous weight function on a locally compact group G.
Since L1(G, omega) has a bounded approximate identity, from Theorem 2.2, approximate amenability and pseudo-amenability are the same for it.
Question 13. Is it true that L1(G, omega) is approximately amenable (pseudo-amenable) if and only if it is amenable?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a locally compact group and $\omega:G\to(0,\infty)$ a continuous weight function, i.e. a continuous function satisfying $\omega(xy)\le \omega(x)\omega(y)$ for all $x,y\in G$ and $\omega(e)=1$. Consider the Beurling algebra
$$L^1(G,\omega)=\Big\{f:G\to\mathbb{C} \text{ measurable} : \|f\|_\omega=\int_G |f(x)|\,\omega(x)\,dx<\infty\Big\},$$
which is a Banach algebra under convolution and the norm $\|\cdot\|_\omega$.

Recall the following notions for a Banach algebra $A$:
\begin{itemize}
\item $A$ is \emph{amenable} if every continuous derivation from $A$ into a dual Banach $A$-bimodule is inner.
\item $A$ is \emph{approximately amenable} if for every Banach $A$-bimodule $X$, every continuous derivation $D:A\to X^*$ is approximately inner; that is, there is a net $(\xi_\alpha)\subset X^*$ with $D(a)=\lim_\alpha (a\cdot \xi_\alpha-\xi_\alpha\cdot a)$ for every $a\in A$.
\item $A$ is \emph{pseudo-amenable} if there exists a (not necessarily bounded) net $(u_\alpha)$ in $A\otimes_\pi A$ such that $a\cdot u_\alpha-u_\alpha\cdot a\to 0$ and $\pi(u_\alpha)a\to a$ for all $a\in A$, where $\pi:A\otimes_\pi A\to A$ is the multiplication map.
\end{itemize}

Since $L^1(G,\omega)$ has a bounded approximate identity, approximate amenability and pseudo-amenability coincide for it.

\textbf{Problem.} Determine whether the following equivalence holds for every locally compact group $G$ and every continuous weight $\omega$ on $G$: the Beurling algebra $L^1(G,\omega)$ is approximately amenable (equivalently, pseudo-amenable) if and only if it is amenable.
artifact.status_search_result: Web searches surface results on amenability and approximate amenability of Beurling algebras (e.g., bounded approximate amenability vs. bounded approximate contractibility on quasi-SIN groups, and the classical characterization that $\ell^1(G,\omega)$ is amenable iff $G$ is amenable and $\omega$ is equivalent to a multiplicative character), but no source confirming or refuting the full equivalence between approximate amenability and amenability of $L^1(G,\omega)$ for arbitrary locally compact $G$ and continuous $\omega$ was found. Status appears unresolved in general.

status_evidence.title: Generalized amenability properties of the Beurling algebras
status_evidence.snippet: Studies bounded approximate amenability and contractibility of Beurling algebras under conditions on the group and weight.
status_evidence.claim: Active research relates approximate amenability variants for Beurling algebras to amenability under additional hypotheses, but a general equivalence is not asserted.

status_evidence.title: Weight functions on groups and an amenability criterion for Beurling algebras
status_evidence.snippet: Amenability criterion: L^1(G,omega) amenable iff G amenable and omega equivalent to a multiplicative character.
status_evidence.claim: The amenability side of the equivalence is classically characterized; the approximate-amenability side is not settled in general.
